ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat discomfort with a sensation of a foreign body and odynophagia following a traumatic event
salient_findings: Persistent sensation of a foreign body in the throat
Protruding lesion through the right palatine tonsil
key_facts: 1-week history of symptoms
History of fish-bone impaction
Denies dysphagia, dyspnea, otalgia, or weight loss
Moderate tobacco use
Habitual betel-nut chewing
Protruding lesion is hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color
No visible fish bone on examination
No mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region on lateral neck radiograph

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil

shortlist.label: Tonsillolithiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region on lateral neck radiograph and history of symptoms following fish-bone impaction

shortlist.label: Calcified tonsillar cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Protruding lesion is hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color, with calcification on radiograph

shortlist.label: Foreign body granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: History of fish-bone impaction and presence of a protruding lesion

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil
shortlist.why_kept: Moderate tobacco use and habitual betel-nut chewing, which are risk factors for squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Tonsillar abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of throat discomfort with a sensation of a foreign body and odynophagia, although no visible abscess is present

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, mobile, well-delineated, and yellowish-white protruding lesion through the right palatine tonsil, combined with a uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region on lateral neck radiograph, is highly suggestive of a tonsillolith, which is a calcified mass that forms on the surface of the tonsils.

rejected.label: Calcified tonsillar cyst
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the lesion and the radiographic findings are more typical of a tonsillolith than a cyst.

rejected.label: Foreign body granuloma
rejected.why: The history of fish-bone impaction could suggest a foreign body reaction, but the lack of visible fish bone and the specific characteristics of the lesion make this less likely.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil
rejected.why: The absence of symptoms such as dysphagia, dyspnea, otalgia, or weight loss, and the well-delineated nature of the lesion, make malignancy less likely.

rejected.label: Tonsillar abscess
rejected.why: The lesion is described as nontender, which is not typical of an abscess, and there's no mention of signs of infection such as fever or significant swelling.
